nodes.summary: The list of the twenty copy sites of the HAMPATH emitter, in this order: the frame sites $f_1u, f_1v, f_2u, f_2v, f_3u, f_3v, f_4u, f_4v$, the row sites $w_1u, w_1v, w_2u, w_2v$, and the detour sites $d_1u, d_1v, d_2u, d_2v, d_3u, d_3v, d_4u, d_4v$.
nodes.title: Copy sites of the HAMPATH emitter, listed

nodes.summary: The list of all pairs of Booleans in the order $(\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{true})$, $(\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false})$, $(\mathrm{false}, \mathrm{true})$, $(\mathrm{false}, \mathrm{false})$.
nodes.title: The four pairs of Booleans

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m$ (the number of clauses), $i$, $x$ and $j$, let $r_{i,l} = m + i(3m + 2) + 1 + l$ be row vertex $l$ of diamond $i$. For a clause $C$, a list of literals, the detours of clause $j$ with contents $C$ in diamond $i$ of variable $x$ are the list of the arcs $(r_{i,3j+1}, j)$ and $(j, r_{i,3j+2})$ if the positive literal $x$ is in $C$, followed by the arcs $(r_{i,3j+2}, j)$ and $(j, r_{i,3j+1})$…
nodes.title: Clause detours in a diamond

nodes.summary: Let $B$ be a natural number and $E$ a list of pairs of natural numbers such that every pair $(u, v)$ in $E$ has $u \le B$ and $v \le B$. Then the bit encoding of $E$, which writes each pair $(u, v)$ as $u$ ones, a zero, $v$ ones and a zero, has length at most $|E| \cdot (2B + 2)$, where $|E|$ is the length of $E$.
nodes.title: Length bound for the bit encoding of an edge list

nodes.summary: The number of extra ones a copy site adds to its counter's value is $1$ for the sites $f_{1v}$, $f_{3u}$, $f_{3v}$, $f_{4v}$, $w_{1v}$, $w_{2u}$, $d_{2v}$ and $d_{3u}$, and $0$ for every other site.
nodes.title: Extra ones of a copy site

nodes.summary: For every list $l$ of natural numbers, folding $l$ from the right into the empty list, prepending each element unless it is already present, gives $l$ with duplicates removed: each element is kept at its last occurrence in $l$, in order.
nodes.title: Removing duplicates by insertion

nodes.summary: In the HAMPATH construction with $m$ clauses, for every diamond $i$ and every $l \in \mathbb{N}$, row vertex $l + 1$ of diamond $i$ is one more than row vertex $l$ of diamond $i$.
nodes.title: Consecutive row vertices

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m$ (the number of clauses) and $i$, write $t_i = m + i(3m + 2)$ for the top of diamond $i$ and $r_{i,l} = t_i + 1 + l$ for its row vertex $l$. Then $t_{i+1} = r_{i,3m} + 1$: the top of diamond $i + 1$ comes right after the last row vertex of diamond $i$.
nodes.title: The next diamond top follows the row

nodes.summary: For a natural number $x$ and a list $V$ of natural numbers, inserting $x$ into $V$ gives $V$ itself if $x$ occurs in $V$, and otherwise the list obtained by prepending $x$ to $V$.
nodes.title: Insert a variable if new

nodes.summary: The counters $p$, $n$, $r$, $j$, $d$ that a copy site of the HAMPATH emitter reads are held on the emitter's stacks $P$, $N$, $R$, $J$, $D$ respectively (the diamond top, the row end, the row vertex, the clause index and the detour vertex).
nodes.title: Stack of a HAMPATH copy-site counter

nodes.summary: The emitter has eighteen distinct stacks: $T$ (the tokens), $O$ (the output), $F$ (the tokens in reading order), $V$ (the distinct variables), $W$ (the other side of the walk over $V$), $Q$ (the edges in progress), $G$ (garbage), $X$ and $Y$ (comparison scratch), $C$ (the clause count), $M$ (three times the clause count), $P$ (the diamond top), $N$ (the row end), $R$ (the row vertex), $L$ (the row loop index), $J$…
nodes.title: Stacks of the HAMPATH emitter

nodes.summary: Let $f$, $p_p$, $p_n$ and $b$ range over bits and $j$ over copy sites. A label of the emitter is one of $\mathrm{a0}$, $\mathrm{anm}$, $\mathrm{aw}(f)$, $\mathrm{ac}(f)$, $\mathrm{ar1}(f)$, $\mathrm{ar2}(f)$, $\mathrm{amv}(f)$, $\mathrm{asep}(f)$, $\mathrm{ab}(f)$, $\mathrm{ad2}$, $\mathrm{ad3}$, $\mathrm{b0}$, $\mathrm{b1}$, $\mathrm{h0}, \dots, \mathrm{h5}$, $\mathrm{r0}, \dots, \mathrm{r4}$, $\mathrm{wi}$,…
nodes.title: Labels of the HAMPATH emitter

nodes.summary: For a copy site $j$ and a bit $b$, the label that follows $j$ is $\mathrm{cpA}(j', b)$, where $j'$ is the site after $j$ in one of the chains $f_{1u}, f_{1v}, f_{2u}, f_{2v}, f_{3u}, f_{3v}, f_{4u}, f_{4v}$, or $w_{1u}, w_{1v}, w_{2u}, w_{2v}$, or $d_{1u}, d_{1v}, d_{2u}, d_{2v}$, or $d_{3u}, d_{3v}, d_{4u}, d_{4v}$. At the ends of the chains it is $\mathrm{r0}$ after $f_{4v}$, $\mathrm{wi}$ after $w_{2v}$ and…
nodes.title: Label after a HAMPATH copy site

nodes.summary: Let $P$ and $Q$ be CNF formulas, $C$ a clause, and $\varphi$ the formula whose clauses are those of $P$, then $C$, then those of $Q$. Write $|P|$ for the number of clauses of $P$ and $\varphi_j$ for clause $j$ of $\varphi$, counting from $0$ (the empty clause if $j$ is out of range). Let $f$ map each natural number $j$ and clause to a list of elements of a type $\alpha$. Then concatenating the lists…
nodes.title: Splitting off the middle clause of a concatenation

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m$ (the number of clauses), $i$ and $l$, let $r_{i,l} = m + i(3m + 2) + 1 + l$ be row vertex $l$ of diamond $i$. The row arcs between row vertices $l$ and $l + 1$ of diamond $i$ are the list of the two arcs $(r_{i,l}, r_{i,l+1})$ and $(r_{i,l+1}, r_{i,l})$.
nodes.title: The row arcs of a diamond

nodes.summary: The type of the twenty copy sites of the emitter machine. Each site writes one endpoint of an edge of the emitted HAMPATH instance, $u$ for the source and $v$ for the target: the sites $f_iu, f_iv$ for $i = 1, \dots, 4$ belong to the four frame edges, $w_iu, w_iv$ for $i = 1, 2$ to the two row edges, and $d_iu, d_iv$ for $i = 1, \dots, 4$ to the detour edges, positive for $i = 1, 2$ and negative for $i = 3, 4$.
nodes.title: Copy sites of the HAMPATH emitter

nodes.summary: The map from copy sites to counters sending $f_1u, f_1v, f_2u, f_3u$ to the diamond top $p$; $f_2v, f_3v, f_4u, f_4v$ to the row end $n$; $w_1u, w_1v, w_2u, w_2v$ to the row vertex $r$; $d_1u, d_2v, d_3u, d_4v$ to the detour vertex $d$; and $d_1v, d_2u, d_3v, d_4u$ to the clause index $j$.
nodes.title: Counter read by a copy site

nodes.summary: The type with the five elements $p, n, r, j, d$, naming the counters of the HAMPATH emitter that a copy site can read: the diamond top $p$, the row end $n$, the row vertex $r$, the clause index $j$ and the detour vertex $d$.
nodes.title: Counters read by HAMPATH copy sites

nodes.summary: For every counter $s$ read by copy sites, the unit symbol of $s$ is the token symbol $\mathrm{cl}$, as a letter of the alphabet of the stack that holds $s$.
nodes.title: Unit symbol of an emitter counter

nodes.summary: The alphabet of the output stack $O$ is the set of bits (booleans); every other stack has the token symbols as its alphabet.
nodes.title: Stack alphabets of the HAMPATH emitter

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
